newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FUN IN BRUSSELS - BAREFOOT DIVA CESARIA EVORA.
newsitem.headline: FUN IN BRUSSELS - BAREFOOT DIVA CESARIA EVORA.

text.p: If you missed her two previous performances in Brussels, the barefoot singer from Cape Verde is back with the rythmic melancholy of her "mornas" next week.

Like the Cape Verde islands, which lie in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Senegal, Cesaria Evora's music is a cross between the sad, slow fados of Portugal and the fast-paced samba rhythm of Brazil.
Sung in Portuguese or the Cape Verde creole, morna lyrics are about longing for home -- there are more Cape Verdians living abroad than on the islands -- faraway lovers and other sad tales.
The songs are traditionally accompanied by acoustic instruments, notably the high-pitched cavaquinho, a small four-string ukele-type guitar.

Evora, born in 1941, grew up singing in the bars of Mindelo, on the Sao Vicente island. Fame came late in life, with a string of performances in France in the mid-90s and the release of her third record "Miss Perfumado", which made her popular well beyong the "world music" market.
"It is thanks to France that I have been able to reach such a large audience," Evora said in a La Sept/Arte documentary which aired last month.
Evora's performances, even though she now sings to large audiences, still echo her early career in bars. She sings, sits down, sips her drink and stands up again for another song.
In solidarity with the impoverished people of her dry and dusty homeland, she always performs barefoot.

For those unable to get tickets for May 26, all her CDs are available from the Mediatheque in Passage 44. "Miss Perfumado", her best, can be hard to find in shops, but "Mar Azul" and "La Diva aux Pieds nues" are also wonderful records. It's maybe best to avoid "Distino di Belita", her first record, which has disco-style electric arrangements which do not fit her style.

If you really want to get into Cape Verdean music, the Mediateque also has CDs of Paulino Vieira, her piano player and musical director, who is a great artist in his own right. There are also CDs of Bana, a Cape Verdian band with a powerful singer. Try the Nha Terra album.
PRACTICAL: Evora sings in the Palais des Beaux Arts, May 26 at 2030, reservations: tel. 507.82.00.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
